items.stem: An analyst needs to stack twelve monthly tables with identical columns into one table. Which Power Query operation fits?

options.rationale: Correct: Append stacks rows from queries that share the same column structure.
Merge joins columns from two queries on a key; it does not stack rows.
Pivot reshapes rows into columns and does not combine separate queries.
Group By aggregates within one query and does not stack tables.

items.explanation: Correct: Append stacks rows from queries that share the same column structure.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the Applied Steps list are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Each step is recorded and can be selected to preview the data at that point
options.rationale: Correct: every transformation is saved as a reviewable step.

options.text: Steps are applied non-destructively to the source data
options.rationale: Correct: the source is not altered; steps transform a working copy.

options.text: Deleting a step always leaves later steps unaffected
options.rationale: Later steps often depend on earlier ones, so deletions can break them.

options.text: The step list runs only once and cannot be refreshed
options.rationale: The step list re-runs on every refresh against current source data.

items.explanation: Correct: every transformation is saved as a reviewable step.

items.stem: Reordering a filter earlier in a query against a SQL source can enable what benefit?

options.text: Query folding, pushing the filter back to the source
options.rationale: Correct: folding translates steps into a source query so less data is pulled.

options.text: Conversion of the query to VBA
options.rationale: Power Query does not convert queries to VBA.

options.text: Removal of the need to refresh
options.rationale: Refresh is still required to pull current data.

items.explanation: Correct: folding translates steps into a source query so less data is pulled.
